newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-CS, Winterthur volatile on merger.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-CS, Winterthur volatile on merger.

text.p: Shares in Swiss merger partners Credit Suisse Group and Winterthur Group were volatile on Tuesday as analysts questioned the short-term benefits of forging one of the world's biggest bank and insurance hybrids.
"I am positive on the long-term deal. But we have downgraded Credit Suisse from buy to hold on short-term uncertainties," said Regina Anhorn from Geneva private bank Lombard Odier.

Credit Suisse registered shares on the Swiss bourse veered between a low of 195.50 Swiss francs, down 4.6 percent, and a high at Monday's close of 205.00 before finishing at 203.50 francs, down 0.7 percent.
CS Holding had lost 1.6 percent on Monday following the merger announcment.
Winterthur fell 5.6 percent to 1,412 Swiss francs then spiked to 1,514 before closing at 1,504, up seven francs or 0.5 percent.
Winterthur had lost 1.1 percent on Monday after gaining 1.9 percent last week and 17 percent since July 1 on takeover speculation.
Traders said selling was caused by doubts about the deal's short-term effects and downgrades by several analysts.

They said buying was led by the BZ Group run by financier Martin Ebner, Winterthur's biggest shareholder by far. Ebner used his 30 percent direct and indirect stake to help force the merger with CS Group.
"As soon as BZ was out of the market again, selling increased," one trader said.
No comment was immediately available from BZ Group.
Under the deal, CS Group will offer 7.3 shares for each Winterthur share and graft the insurer to the group as a separate operational unit still under the name Winterthur.
Bank Vontobel downgraded CS Group from a strong buy to a buy. UBS also cut CS Group, from buy to hold

"After the merger announcement, we think price euphoria has been capped and we recommend a switch to Swiss Bank Corp, which is better valued based on fundamentals," UBS analyst Daniel Haeuselmann wrote in a research report.
Haeuselmann said the downgrade was based on the high valuation of CS Group shares and profit dilution forecast this year and next due to the deal.

"The size of the transaction (Winterthur is valued at 14.1 billion Swiss francs) and the comparatively low synergies at net profit level -- after tax -- of 210 million Swiss francs over three years make us cautious," he wrote in a research report.
Lomard Odier's Anhorn also viewed the company's forecast of synergies -- between 300 million and 350 million Swiss francs over three years -- as modest and too fragmented.
Anhorn also said she was not sure how much progress CS Group had made in a major restructuring plan just started this year, aimed at trimmming costs and boosting profitability.
"I'd prefer to see some results from the ongoing restructuring at Credit Suisse before they go a step further," she said.
"There is a lot to do on various levels, and that brings it down again to the timing...why are they doing it now after the Winterthur shareprice has gone up a lot?" Ahorn said.
Analysts said another uncertainty was what investor Ebner would do with his Winterthur stake. Ebner has called the CS Group offer fair but has not explicitly said he accepts.
For the longer term, there were more positive reactions.
"I think my initial view that is it probably a modest positive still stands," said John Leonard from Salomon Brothers in London.

"The quality of earnings at Credit Suisse clearly goes up, because of conservative accounting at Winterthur but also because the business, particularly the life assurance business, is more stable than the Credit Suisse average," he said.
